A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TULIP and retain the same core method and experiments. All 16 pages of v1 and 24 pages of v2, including appendix figures, tables and equations, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original TULIP retrieval results, ablations, attention analyses and generated-image examples, including appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds human evaluation, compositional benchmarks, DOCCI retrieval and training-data ablation results in Tables 5–8.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.4 retain the same RoPE replacement, cosine distillation, NTK-aware context expansion and combined short/long contrastive objective. Additional evaluations and ablation controls do not change the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Appendices A.3–A.4 newly evaluate ARO and VL-Checklist compositional understanding and DOCCI long-caption retrieval. DOCCI was only discussed in v1. These extend task and dataset coverage beyond the retained COCO, Flickr30k, Long-DCI, ShareGPT4V and Urban-1K evaluations.

E2.justification: Generation comparisons expand beyond CLIP and Long-CLIP to the T5-based PIXART-Alpha and ELLA systems in Figure 3 and the appendix. Table 3 also adds an absolute-positional-encoding control. The original retrieval comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix A.2 adds randomized pairwise image-alignment judgments from 15 annotators on 20 samples, reported as win rates. A.5 adds training conditions using 33%, 66% and 100% of ShareGPT4V. Original main-experiment settings remain unchanged; A.5's 1.2-million-pair description does not establish a change to the retained main-text 1-million-pair training setting.

E4.justification: Table 3 extends the positional-encoding ablation with an absolute-encoding control. Appendix A.5 investigates dependence on student-training data volume, while A.7 adds retrieval case studies highlighting fine-grained errors. Existing context-length, loss-function and attention analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new human study supplies annotator and sample counts but reports only point-estimate win rates, without uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Original retrieval tables and existing ablation scores remain unchanged. New results include 89% versus 11% human preference for TULIP versus CLIP, DOCCI image-to-text/text-to-image R@1 of 77.9/79.1 versus Long-CLIP's 66.5/78.5, compositional and data-volume results, absolute-encoding scores, and revised qualitative comparisons.

T1.justification: The problem definitions, rotary-attention equations, distillation objective and combined contrastive objective remain unchanged in Sections 3.1–3.4 and Equations 1–4. Neither version adds formal propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about extending CLIP's context, two-stage adaptation, Long-DCI and improved retrieval/generation. Added supporting evaluations do not redefine these central contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations about data-volume dependence and T5-comparable generation with plug-and-play advantages; existing mechanism explanations and limitations remain. A.3 newly claims consistent superiority over CLIP, although Table 6 shows lower ARO Flickr scores, 52.3 versus 60.2, and COCO scores, 43.9 versus 47.9.

D1.justification: The abstract supplies a repository link and states code availability, replacing v1's future-release promise. Table 4 clarifies that its unchanged results precede position expansion, and Appendix A.2 provides annotator instructions. Core training hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations for PIXART-Alpha, ELLA, T5, ARO and VL-Checklist, and positions TULIP against T5-based generation systems. Existing positional-encoding and contrastive-model positioning largely remains; DOCCI's publication update represents the same cited work.

P1.justification: Main-section order and most prose remain intact. Changes include localized wording and header edits, a revised generation discussion in Section 4.2, and named appendix subsections organizing the additional evaluations.

P2.justification: Figure 3 changes from a three-method display to five-method comparisons, with its six original cases retained across appendix Figures 7–8. The standalone appendix gallery is substantially replaced by comparison grids, with some examples reused. New tables, human-study illustrations and retrieval panels substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: The human study, T5 comparisons, additional benchmarks and diagnostic ablations strengthen support beyond v1's selected generation examples and existing retrieval results. Code-access information also improves. The net gain is limited by the 20-sample human study without uncertainty estimates and the new compositional-superiority claim contradicted by Table 6. These additions provide useful validation, but their reporting limitations temper the overall improvement.
